name: Central Square (Government Square)
note: Ceremonial square of the Soviet centre (city-centre anchor); Irad Day parades, Government House, museum and post office front it.

name: Government House
note: Seat of the ISEZ executive (de jure); 1992 riders cordoned it and Central Square; placed on the square.

name: Legislative Hall
note: Meeting place of the 60-seat Mejlis (Territorial Legislature) since Oct 1992; in the government district of the Soviet centre.

name: Hall of Justice (Supreme Court of Irad)
note: Granite neoclassical court building on Liberty Boulevard housing the five-justice Supreme Court; Swiss band marched from it to the museum on the central square.

name: Talas District Court
note: Trial court created by the 2003 Judicial Reforms Act; Tulparcoin and Kyzyl-Jyldyz cases; placed near the centre.

name: Talas City Hall
note: Seat of the Talas city council (transport committee, budget papers); placed on the central square.

name: Bank of Irad head office
note: Currency-board monetary authority issuing the som; houses the interbank clearing house.

name: Silk Road Financial Tower (Talasbank HQ)
note: Headquarters of Talasbank, the largest commercial bank; on the central-avenue tower strip.

name: Altyn Tower
note: Tallest building in Irad (2016, 27 storeys, base-isolated) on the central avenue skyline built by Alikhan's and Adil's firms; Altyn Tower Pizza is a Tulpar delivery partner.

name: Miners' Hall
note: Soviet-era miners' union building in central Talas, seat of the Iradi National Chamber of Mining and Metallurgy.
wiki: Iradi National Chamber of Mining and Metallurgy

name: General Staff complex
note: Headquarters of the State Defense Corps (MKK) in Talas; placed NE of the centre.

name: Central City Park
note: Main park of the Soviet centre; the 1971 berkutchi statue stands at its entrance.

name: The Hunter's Vigil
note: 1971 bronze kneeling berkutchi with golden eagle, ~4 m, on a granite plinth at the entrance to the central city park.

name: Widow's Horse Memorial
note: Bronze riderless horse (1996) near the site of the former collective-farm market where the 14 June 1956 checkpoint shooting happened; vigils every 14 June.

name: Talas Central Post Office
note: Neoclassical 1954 building on the central square; international mail sorting via the Kazakh postal service.

name: National Historical Museum of Irad
note: Former 1909 Russian gymnasium on the central square; national history and archaeology museum (140,000 objects).

name: Talas Philharmonic Hall ("Tündük")
note: Round 1971-74 concert hall under a ribbed shell (Erkin Sydykbekov), home of the Talas Symphony Orchestra; listed 2021.

name: Talas Opera and Ballet Theater
note: Soviet-era opera and ballet house (Venera Kasymova prima 1971-90); placed in the Soviet centre.

name: Talas State Academic Drama Theatre
note: Staged The Last Pass in 1967; placed on the central avenue.

name: Talas municipal theater (Town Hall Meeting site)
note: Where the 11 Mar 1992 Town Hall Meeting proclaimed the Republic and the Alimbekov-Baker Treaty was signed in the basement on 2 Jun 1992.

name: National Conservatory of Folk Music
note: Music conservatory in Talas (Aida Temirova's piano department).

name: Cinema Boulevard
note: Boulevard of cinemas hosting the biennial Talas International Film Festival; site of the national film archive.

name: Talasfilm Archives and Film Preservation Institute
note: National film archive on Cinema Boulevard (separated from the studio 1995).

name: Talasfilm Studios
note: Feature-film studio founded 1954; works mainly for IradOne since 2007.

name: Alikhan Media Center (IradOne HQ)
note: IradOne headquarters and studios in downtown Talas since 2017.

name: IradOne Transmitter Mast (Television Hill)
note: 220 m guyed mast (1972) on Television Hill; placed on the first foothill rise south of the city.

name: Communications Square (Attelkom HQ)
note: Square with Attelkom's glass headquarters (2002) in the western corridor toward the air base.

name: Köhne Diz (Talas citadel)
note: Kokand fortress of the 1820s on a 14 m mound above the Talas River, core of the Old City; Russian grid town laid out east of it.

name: Kalan Darwaza
note: South gate of the citadel, pointed brick arch rebuilt 1820s, restored 2002.

name: Temir-Kapka Gate
note: Only surviving Kokand-era gate (1820s, iron-plated doors) at the northern entrance to the Old Quarter; city symbol.

name: Coppersmiths' Row (Misgaron)
note: Vaulted 19th-century trading row in the Old Quarter.

name: Bazar-i Kalan
note: Covered central market (1950s hall) on the eastern edge of the Old Citadel Quarter; money changers, potato prices.

name: Juma Mosque (Talas)
note: 1890s mosque with columned wooden porch in the Old Talas Citadel Quarter; closed in the 1930s, reopened.

name: Church of St. Yuhanna (Talas)
note: Syro-Iradi parish church built 1908 in the Old Citadel Quarter, carved screen by Almazbek Kasymov.

name: Sarchashma Springs and bathhouse
note: Springs at the foot of the citadel terrace feeding fountains and a Kokand-era domed bathhouse (restored 2014).

name: Iradi Telegraph Office
note: 1879 brick Tashkent-Verny telegraph station in the Old Quarter; Attelkom switching node since 1999.

name: Kara-Khanid minaret foundations
note: Excavated 11th-century minaret foundations beside a Christian cemetery with Syriac gravestones in the Old Quarter.

name: Jibek Jolu clothing market
note: Clothing market hit by an August 2026 fire; stallholders suing operator Jibek Jolu Trade.

name: Talas Central Bus Station
note: Intercity terminal: buses/marshrutkas to Nurzhan, Semiz, Kara-Bulak, Kyzyl-Adyr, Sary-Bulak, Tash-Kömür, Iyık Janyl; placed between bazaar and centre.

name: Talas Municipal Bus Depot
note: Main garage and dispatch yard of the city bus company (260 buses, 34 routes) opened 1968.

name: Talas railway station
note: Terminus of the Talas branch of Irad Temir Jolu; daily passenger train to Nurzhan (~7 h by the lowland route).

name: Silk Road Arena
note: 21,000-seat home of Tulpar Talas and the national team; the 1956 Dinamo Stadium rebuilt 2014 by TCDG.

name: Irad State Hippodrome
note: 25,000-seat equestrian stadium (Soviet Central Hippodrome), HQ of the National Equestrian Sports Directorate; ulak league and President's Cup.

name: Irad Central Sports Complex
note: 6,500-seat indoor arena (1979 republican sports palace); wrestling, futsal cup.

name: Attelkom Park
note: Home ground of Attelkom Talas FC; placed near the Attelkom HQ in the western corridor.

name: TSU Stadium
note: Home ground of Universitet Talas on the university campus.

name: Talas State University
note: Oldest and largest university (1958, ~18,400 students); 2023 protests began here; campus placed SE of the centre.

name: State Archives of Irad
note: National archive in a 1997 purpose-built repository on the TSU campus (fonds 3, 85, 108...).

name: Talas Pedagogical Institute
note: Teacher-training institute, basis of TSU in 1958; Ishakov studied here.

name: Talas Gendarmerie Academy
note: Officer school of the Republican Gendarmerie; site of Ruslan Toktarov's Dec 2024 "guests" speech.

name: Talas Veterinary Research Center
note: State veterinary lab (1962); DNA parentage testing for the Akyel and Chongtor studbooks.

name: Talas Regional Hospital Medical Complex
note: Main referral and teaching hospital of the ISEZ (opened 1954, rebuilt 1995-2002).

name: Talas Municipal Hospital No. 1
note: Main city emergency hospital, 480 beds (1964).

name: Talas Blood Services Center
note: Former republican transfusion station (1958), supplies the regional hospital blood bank.

name: St. Luka Clinic
note: Free outpatient and dental clinic of the St. Luka Community Health Mission in the southern districts (1997).

name: St. Luka Hospital
note: Mission hospital to which the St. Luka Clinic refers patients.

name: St. Maryam Catholic Academy
note: Secondary school (2001) run by the Sisters of the Cross of Irad.

name: Talas Municipal Gymnasium No. 4
note: Selective English-specialized school (1936) with its own riding programme at the Hippodrome.

name: Talas American School
note: US-curriculum school (1994); placed by the Alatau Heights returnee suburb SE of the centre.

name: Talas Youth Soccer Academy
note: Youth football academy (1997) with US college coaches.

name: Church of St. Tomas (Talas)
note: Latin-model church (nave, pews, spire) built 1996 with American Catholic charities.

name: Talas Pre-Trial Detention Center
note: Remand prison of the Corrections Directorate; placed in the northern district.

name: Talas women's colony
note: Women's correctional colony near Talas; placed NE outskirts.

name: Talas Municipal Fire Brigade HQ
note: HQ of seven fire stations, ~420 firefighters, in the city centre.

name: Talas Fire Station No. 2
note: Covers the western districts and the TAEZ; ammonia-leak trained (1979).

name: Talas Municipal Water Treatment Works
note: Surface-water plant drawing from the Talas River (1972), supplies the northern districts; partly solar-powered.

name: Talas city landfill
note: Landfill opened 1981 north-west of the city, near capacity (Talas Public Sanitation Works).

name: Talas Municipal Cold Storage
note: 1976 Soviet kholodilnik in the northern industrial district; winter food reserve.

name: Talas Free Economic Trade Zone
note: Bonded industrial park (2009) on the northern outskirts: garments, assembly, warehouses.

name: Talas Customs Clearance Terminal
note: Bonded freight terminal in the Free Economic Trade Zone, X-ray scanners since 2015, ~41,000 containers (2023).

name: Iradi Leatherworks Factory
note: 1958 shoe and harness factory, privatized 1996; boots for security services, saddlery.

name: Talas Dairy Processing Combine
note: Cooperative dairy (1964): milk, kefir, suzma, bottled kymyz.

name: Talas Agribusiness Export Zone (TAEZ)
note: Bonded food-processing park (1998) on the old fattening complex land west of Semiz; SuKarne, Conagra, cold chain; rail sidings.

name: Sukarne Irad Complex
note: SuKarne slaughterhouse and packing plant (1999), >150,000 head/yr, halal line; in the western industrial corridor.

name: Sukarne Feedlot Complex
note: ~50,000-head feedlot west of Semiz on the former Talas State Cattle-Fattening Complex.

name: Sukarne Quality Control Labs
note: Food-safety and export-certification labs (1999).

name: Conagra Talas Beef Facility
note: US beef-packing and cold-storage plant in the TAEZ.

name: Talas Cold Chain Logistics Hub
note: 25,000 m2 refrigerated warehouse and rail terminal in the TAEZ (reefer trains to Kazakhstan and Russia).

name: Talas Central Cattle Mart
note: Weekend livestock market on the western edge near the TAEZ; separate horse section.

name: Church of St. Yusup the Worker
note: Semiz parish (consecrated 2005), Sunday Spanish Roman-rite Mass, Guadalupe chapel (2006); sheltered people in 2007.

name: Semiz market (el mercado)
note: Daily market of the Mexican district, biggest on Saturday.

name: Semiz water tower
note: Landmark water tower of the 1974 fattening-complex blocks in central Semiz.

name: Lienzo Charro de Semiz
note: Charro arena (2009) on the la Colonia (south) side; hosts the Eki Eldin At Oyunu horse games each September.

name: Semiz cemetery
note: Orthodox, Korean and Catholic sections; marigolds and riderless-horse procession on 1-2 Nov.

name: Talas Air Base
note: 12 km W of Talas on the southern terrace of the Talas River; 3,400 m runway; US forces, MKK air wing, civil aprons; built 1952.

name: Talas Airport Logistics Hub (Iradiya terminal)
note: Bonded air-cargo terminal and Iradiya hangars on the civil (southern) aprons beside the base.

name: Barysh Rapid Reaction Strike Group base
note: Gendarmerie strike group stationed next to Talas Air Base, guarding the outer perimeter.

name: Talas Air Base foothill radar stations
note: Radar and flight-tracking stations in the Talas Alatau foothills monitoring the valley-steppe corridor.

name: 1st Mechanized Infantry Brigade base
note: MKK brigade "outside Talas" covering the Talas valley and western Qara-Chik sector.

name: Kand-i Kohna
note: Saka-to-9th-century town mound on a Talas River terrace about 6 km W of central Talas.

name: Kashkar-Aryk
note: Spring-fed stream rising below the Old Quarter terrace, ~5 km through gardens to the Talas; reopening planned 2019.

name: Caravanserai of Rabat-i-Safed
note: 9th-c. Sogdian white-limestone caravanserai 25 km E of Talas on the medieval road toward the Chu; UNESCO Silk Roads component 2014; open-air museum, Kara-Khanid coins found 2026.

name: Kok-Tash Kariz System
note: ~140 km of karez galleries beneath the Talas Alatau fans east of Talas (Kand-i Nau, Sabz-Kand); UNESCO Silk Roads component 2014; smuggling galleries near the line.

name: Kand-i Nau
note: Kara-Khanid walled-town mound at the lower end of a Kok-Tash kariz branch in the foothills E of Talas, beside Jangy-Kent.

name: Shelji
note: Medieval silver-mining town (8th-12th c.) on a terrace of the upper Talas in eastern Talas District beside Kümüshtü; valley floor ~1,800 m near here.

name: Taldy-Bulak petroglyphs
note: Bronze Age to Turkic petroglyphs on boulders in the lower (ISEZ) part of a side valley SE of Talas.

name: Jety-Kaiyng
note: Red sandstone cliffs and pillars ("seven bulls of Morkhan") with a birch grove, northern foothills SE of Talas; day-trip site.

name: State Stud Farm of Talas
note: Government Akyel/Chongtor stud ~15 km E of Talas; stallion Zharkyn stands here.

name: Chong-Talas Stud Farm
note: Akyel Syndicate stud on the Talas River ~20 km upstream of Talas (founded 1924), cradle of the Akyel revival.

name: Akyel Breeding Sanctuary
note: Fenced breeding estate of Governor Toktarov's foundation mares in the Talas Alatau foothills (closed to public).

name: Kyzyl-Jyldyz stud
note: Private stud "near Talas" of Kanat Ormonbekov, centre of the 2022 DNA-substitution fraud.

name: Arstanov stud farm
note: Stud set up 1993 by Keneshbek Arstanov in the Talas valley where Zharkyn was foaled (2010).

name: Talas Solar Park (Boz-Tektir)
note: 50 MW tracking PV plant (2021, ~120 ha) on the dry Boz-Tektir terrace above the middle Talas valley.

name: Boz-Tektir
note: Dry grey steppe terrace above the canals of the middle Talas valley; rain-fed wheat and the solar park.

name: Kara-Bulak Grain Logistics Depot
note: NAI silo complex (1968, ~150,000 t) beside the rail line at Kara-Bulak, 35 km W of Talas.

name: Kara-Bulak station
note: Station on the Talas line serving the grain depot; sells lucerne (26 som a bale).

name: Kara-Bulak maize station
note: Soviet maize-breeding station founded 1956 for the yellow dent feed-maize drive.

name: Kara-Bulak kurgans
note: Burial mounds near Kara-Bulak open to visitors.

name: Urmaral River (Tegirmen confluence)
note: Cold Talas Alatau tributary joining the Talas from the south W of the capital at Tegirmen; trout farms.

name: Kashka-Suu River (lower course)
note: Glacier-fed left tributary of the Talas in Talas District; three small (<2 MW) HPPs built in the 2010s.

name: Muz-Suu River (canal intakes)
note: 26 km glacier river joining the Talas in Talas District; two canal intakes; 2016 GLOF damaged Tash-Bulak.

name: Qara-Chik Border Checkpoint
note: Main crossing of the demarcation line (~1,900 crossings/day) at about 1,220 m at the mouth of the Kara-Buura valley, ~2 km above Qara-Chik and ~15 km by road from Kyzyl-Adyr (~75 km from Talas): the road on into the tribal Chatkal valley and down to the Fergana valley; El-Choro post 1 km up the valley.

name: UNMI Headquarters, Kara-Oi
note: Former Soviet agricultural research station on the ISEZ side between Talas and the line, at the end of the Talas – Kara-Oi road; Joint Liaison Committee, 2011 summit.

name: Besh-Tash National Park
note: 1996 park in the Besh-Tash valley ~20 km S of Talas; core of a 32,400 ha conservation area; lower valley ISEZ, upper valley and lakes ATR.

name: Besh-Tash Ranger Headquarters
note: Park entrance and visitor centre at Kök-Oi, mouth of the Besh-Tash valley, ~20 km S of Talas at ~1,200 m.

name: Besh-Tash Timber Concession
note: Spruce-thinning and dead-juniper lease in the lower valley buffer zone ~20 km S of Talas.

name: Besh-Tash Lower Tarn
note: Turquoise moraine lake at ~2,400 m among spruce below the Upper Lake.

name: Besh-Tash Upper Lake (Lake Besh-Tash)
note: Largest cirque lake at ~3,000 m, >28 m deep, at the valley head; tribal side, visits via UN liaison.

name: Yusup Ayyubov house-museum
note: Painter's house-studio and museum at Besh-Tash; canon says "Besh-Tash (upper valley; Ayyubov museum)", aligned with the settlements file's Besh-Tash village at the valley mouth beside Kök-Oi.

name: Kemel Ishakov house-museum
note: Novelist's birthplace museum (2012) and grave in Arsha-Say, below the Talas Alatau in Talas District.

name: Kara-Suu Canyon
note: 32 km limestone gorge (walls to 650 m) south of Talas carrying the Sary-Bulak road to the antimony works and the Chatkal smelter; lower canyon ISEZ (Sary-Bulak District), upper valley ATR.

name: Kara-Suu Canyon petroglyphs
note: Hundreds of petroglyphs on varnished boulders near the canyon entrance (unprotected).

name: Kara-Suu cave chapel
note: Cave chapel proposed as the First Church of Janyl; monks hid Iyık Janyl manuscripts in canyon caves in the 1930s.

name: Kara-Suu Hydroelectric Station
note: 18 MW run-of-river station (early 1960s) in the lower Kara-Suu Canyon, weir-tunnel-penstock; feeds the Sary-Bulak corridor.

name: Kara-Suu Canyon checkpoint (State Route 1 northern post)
name_ru: КПП у входа в ущелье Кара-Суу
note: Gendarmerie control post where the Sary-Bulak road enters the canyon (~13 km SW of Talas), inside the ISEZ.

name: Sary-Bulak Antimony Works (SBAW)
note: Antimony mine (1961) in the Sary-Bulak Gorge ~20 km SSW of Talas (~24 km by road); ~2,300 staff; phased restart planned 2026-27.

name: Sary-Bulak Gorge
note: Steep limestone gorge ~20 km SSW of Talas lined with the shafts and dumps of SBAW; haul road and rail spur on its floor.

name: Chatkal Chemical Smelting Complex
note: Antimony smelter (1961-64, ~2,200 staff) in the Talas Alatau foothills ~30 km SW of Talas; ingots and trioxide for China.

name: Chatkal Antimony Processing Mill
note: Flotation mill beside the smelter (1964), ~30 km SW of Talas.

name: Chatkal Rare Earth Facility
note: By-product plant at the smelter recovering bismuth and tellurium (no rare-earth ore).

name: Chatkal Tailings Repository
note: Soviet-era tailings dam of the Chatkal complex (antimony, arsenic), embankment raised late 2000s.

name: Chatkal Mountain Rescue Base
note: Mine and mountain rescue station (1972) near the Chatkal smelter.

name: Chatkal Primary Health Post
note: Clinic for smelter families and nearby villages (lung and arsenic screening).

name: Kemer Antimony Mine
note: Underground stibnite mine (1970s) 12 km W of the main Sary-Bulak mine, in the foothills SW of Talas facing the Chatkal.

name: Kyzyl-Jar Antimony Shafts
note: Two small shafts in southern Sary-Bulak District close to the line; closed 2007-11.

name: Maryam-Bulak
note: Karst spring (25 L/s, 9 °C) venerated as St. Maryam's spring, with an 1890s chapel restored 1995; late-summer pilgrimage, rain prayers.

name: Ak-Kyr
note: 11 km Silurian limestone ridge S of Talas rising to ~2,100 m; lime quarry at its W end.

name: Kyrk-Kazyk Caves
note: 1.8 km karst cave in Ak-Kyr; largest horseshoe-bat colony in Irad; natural monument since 2004.

name: Chatkal Wildlife Protection Post
note: Ranger station in upper Sary-Bulak District facing the Chatkal range across the line.

name: Sary-Bulak Mountain Rifle Battalion
note: MKK battalion covering the industrial corridor S of Talas.

name: Otmek Tunnel
note: ~5 km tunnel (2003) under the Otmek crest on State Route 1, portals at about 3,150-3,200 m, some 150 m below the Ötmök pass (3,330 m), whose old road is kept as a summer bypass. Inside the ISEZ State Route 1 corridor since the 2009 protocol.

name: Fergana Gateway
note: The real Ala-Bel pass (3,184 m) on the road from the Suusamyr valley down the Chychkan valley to the Toktogul basin: the gateway from the Talas side to the Fergana side. Moved here to follow the real road (was a 2,480 m saddle in the lore). Inside the ISEZ State Route 1 corridor since the 2009 protocol.

name: Fergana Gateway summit checkpoint
note: Gendarmerie checkpoint where bus passengers' IDs are checked. Inside the ISEZ State Route 1 corridor since the 2009 protocol; an internal control post, not a line crossing.

name: Toktogul Dam and Hydroelectric Station
note: 215 m concrete gravity dam, four units, 1,200 MW (refit to 1,440 MW reported 2026); dam and powerhouse transferred to the ISEZ under the 2009 Toktogul basin and State Route 1 corridor protocol; Gendarmerie guard since October 2009.

name: Toktogul Reservoir
note: ~19 km3 reservoir filling the Toktogul (Ketmen-Töbö) basin; record low 2008.

name: Toktogul switchyard and national dispatch centre
name_ir: Toktogul bölüshtürüü jayy jana dispetcherlik borboru
name_ru: Распредустройство Токтогульской ГЭС и национальный диспетчерский центр
note: High-voltage switchyard and grid dispatch centre on the ISEZ side below the dam, passed by State Route 1; all export lines start here.

name: Naryn bridge checkpoint (below Toktogul dam)
note: Gendarmerie checkpoint where State Route 1 crosses the Naryn below the dam; an internal control post inside the State Route 1 corridor since 2009.

name: Kurpsai Hydroelectric Station
note: Next station of the Naryn cascade below Toktogul, in the ISEZ Lower Naryn corridor.

name: Tash-Kömür Hydroelectric Station
note: Cascade station near the town (begun 1980s, last units late 1990s).

name: Shamaldy-Sai Hydroelectric Station
note: Lower cascade station near the edge of the Fergana Valley.

name: Uch-Kurgan Hydroelectric Station
note: First-built (1950s-60s) and lowest cascade station at the edge of the Fergana Valley.

name: Tash-Kömür airstrip
note: Soviet airstrip lengthened to ~1,900 m in 2009; subsidized Iradiya service to Talas.

name: Tash-Kömür coal mines
note: Coal mines (from the early 1930s) on the gorge slopes above the town.

name: UNMI Lower Naryn sector HQ
note: UN observer sector headquarters at Tash-Kömür; Naryn Protocol consent reached here in 2022.

name: Lower Naryn Mountain Rifle Battalion
note: MKK battalion guarding the cascade stations and the south end of State Route 1.

name: Lower Naryn district hospital
note: District hospital in Tash-Kömür.

name: Jyluu-Bulak sanatorium
note: 42 °C sulfurous springs on a fault in a side valley of the Naryn above Tash-Kömür; 1968 sanatorium, private since 1997.

name: Altyn-Bulak mineral water plant
note: Carbonated iron-rich springs and 1978 bottling plant in the foothills N of Tash-Kömür.

name: Church of St. Janyl
note: 1727 domed cathedral (consecrated 1730) on Cathedral Hill, the spur above the city; 22 m turquoise dome; UNESCO 2004 with Shar-i-Kuhna; mother see.

name: Cathedral Hill
note: Spur occupied by the old town and cathedral precinct; armed units do not enter the precinct; esplanade for the Blessing of the Herds.

name: Iyık Janyl Monastic Cloister
note: Walled 18th-19th-c. cloister of contemplative monks beside the cathedral (14 monks).

name: St. Ephrem Major Seminary (Cathedral Seminary)
note: Seminary in the cloister beside the cathedral (1730s school; closed 1937, reopened 1994).

name: Cathedral Seminary Library of Iyık Janyl
name_ir: Iyık Janyl Sobor Seminariyasynyn Koljazma Kitepkanasy
note: Manuscript library founded 1732 (Syriac, Sogdian, Christian Turkic).
wiki: Cathedral Seminary Library of Iyık Janyl

name: Iyık Janyl Diocesan Archives Vault
note: Climate-controlled vault (2006) below the chapter house beside the cathedral.

name: Iyık Janyl Pilgrimage Hostel
note: 180-bed hostel (1999) in a restored 19th-c. caravanserai near the cathedral.

name: Irad Palace of Art
note: Leading gallery (1996) in a former Soviet house of culture near the cathedral; holds The White Rider Shows the Way.

name: Motherhouse of the Order of St. Janyl the Hermit
note: Motherhouse on the edge of the Naryn gorge below Cathedral Hill, south of the city, with farm terraces.
wiki: Order of St. Janyl the Hermit

name: Ruins of Old Iyık Janyl (Shar-i-Kuhna)
note: 11th-14th-c. walled Christian town (~45 ha, basilica 38x24 m) on a river terrace 3 km S of the city centre, west of the Naryn; UNESCO 2004.

name: Diz-i Safid
note: Kara-Khanid hilltop citadel on a limestone knoll rising ~140 m from the western flats in the middle of the city, refortified 1720s; overlooks the Lower Town and the Naryn.

name: Khunuk Creek
note: Cold spring-fed creek from the Fergana Range foothills through the Shahr-i Khunuk summer quarter to the Naryn above the city.

name: Talas North Terminal
note: Combined rail-road crossing into Kazakhstan on the frontier facing Shymkent, where the Trans-Talas Highway (the old M39) and the Kara-Buura railway leave Irad; the only protocol crossing for trains; Trans-Chuy runs most traffic.

name: Kyzyl-Adyr Reservoir
note: Former Kirov Reservoir (1975, ~550 million m3) on the Talas near Kyzyl-Adyr; releases counted in the 2021 Kazakh water share.

name: Ak-Tash Training Center
note: State Defense Corps conscript basic-training centre outside Ak-Tash village in the western Talas Alatau foothills; kariz-watered fields.

name: Ak-Tash sanatorium
note: Small Soviet trade-union sanatorium at a warm mineral spring in the valley above Ak-Tash.

name: Ak-Tilek Ranch
note: Private Akyel x Thoroughbred racing stud (2009) in the lower Talas valley.

name: Kyzyl-Adyr district hospital
note: Hospital of the Kara-Buura district centre.

name: Kyzyl-Adyr Hills
note: Red loess hills rising 150-300 m south of the town; rain-fed barley, shelter-strip programme.

name: Ambar-Döbö
note: River terrace on the southern side of the lower Talas valley with ~60 Kara-Khanid grain pits excavated 1990.

name: Karool-Döbö
note: 60 m bluff at the Kenkol-Talas confluence near Ming-Örük with a Kara-Khanid watchtower and Kokand post.

name: Kenkol burial ground
note: 1st-4th-c. Hunnic catacomb cemetery on terraces above Ming-Örük where the Kenkol leaves the mountains.

name: Kuru-Say
note: Dry wash draining 35 km north across the lower valley; April 1998 flood cut the Trans-Talas Highway (bridge rebuilt 2001).

name: Ichke-Suu Gorge
note: 9 km relict sea-buckthorn gorge on the N slopes of the western Talas Alatau; lower end ISEZ, upper end ATR.

name: Kapka-Bel
note: Low saddle on the northern side of the lower Talas valley, old caravan entrance from the Chu plains, Kokand customs-post foundations.

name: Eski-Korgon fort
note: 1830s Kokand mudbrick fort guarding the old road down the lower valley toward the Kazakh border.

name: Ak-Döbö settlement mound
note: 6 m ashy mound with Late Bronze Age Andronovo pit-houses (rescue dig 1984).

name: Talas Alatau
note: Range (~270 km) forming the south side of the Talas valley, Kyrgyz Range junction to Pskem/Ugam; label point on the central crest.

name: Manas Peak
note: Highest summit of the Talas Alatau (4,482 m) at its western end where it meets the Pskem/Ugam ranges; undemarcated Uzbek border on the massif.

name: Manas Glacier
note: 2.6 km benchmark glacier on the north flank; snout ~3,600 m, retreated ~450 m since 1970.

name: Manas Peak Glaciological Observatory
note: Research station (1964) at 3,850 m on the NW ridge (Nazira Isaeva); helipad, seismometer vault.

name: Kök-Suu Peak
note: Granite peak (3,890 m) on the main ridge between the head of the Kara-Buura valley and the Chatkal basin.

name: Kara-Buura Pass
note: Pass at the head of the Kara-Buura valley leading over the range to the upper Chatkal.

name: Kara-Buura River
note: Rises on the tribal side of the western Talas Alatau and flows north into the lower valley, almost wholly taken for irrigation.

name: Rabat-i Sangin
note: Kara-Khanid boulder-and-lime caravanserai in the upper Kara-Buura valley on the old route to the Chatkal.

name: Kenkol Pass
note: Pass at ~2,850 m at the head of the Kenkol valley; 1960s graded military road; line runs close; 2009 mine killed two UNMI observers.

name: Kenkol Mountain Meteorological Post
note: Weather station (1936, automated 2011) near the Kenkol Pass on the ISEZ side.

name: Chong-Kenkol
note: Upper Kenkol gorge with dense Tian Shan spruce protected by the clan council.

name: Kara-Koyun Valley
note: Karakoyun clan homeland and winter gathering place south of Kara-Buura District beyond the line, on the road from the Qara-Chik checkpoint to the Chatkal valley; extraordinary kurultai venue.

name: Karakoyun Pass
note: Pass of about 3,050 m at the head of the Kara-Koyun Valley carrying the clans' seasonal gravel road from the Qara-Chik checkpoint into the Chatkal valley; Karakoyun flocks cross in June and September.

name: Grave of Muratbek Biy
note: Stone enclosure near the Karakoyun Pass venerated as the grave of the 18th-century clan leader.

name: Urmaral Tarns
note: Chain of three glacial lakes (2,900-3,100 m) at the head of the Urmaral valley; middle lake monitored for GLOF.

name: Kyzyl-Köl
note: Moraine-dammed turquoise glacial lake at ~2,800 m among reddish rocks in the Talas Alatau.

name: Kara-Suu Rapids
note: 150 m of cascades over 2 km in a granite cleft just above the Chong-Kapka gorge on the upper Kara-Suu.

name: Kara-Suu Gold Prospecting Area
note: Artisanal placer panning on gravel bars of the upper Kara-Suu under adat (no mercury or dredging).

name: Kara-Suu Rural Health Center
note: Solar-powered six-bed clinic (2014) in the upper Kara-Suu valley serving ~9,000 herders.

name: Kara-Suu Tribal Elders Council Hall
note: Octagonal yurt-plan wooden hall (2010) for adat hearings; venue of extraordinary winter kurultai.

name: Tegerek-Köl
note: Near-circular bedrock cirque lake (420 m across, 31 m deep) at ~3,150 m; low outburst risk.

name: Köl-Sai glacial lake
note: Moraine-dammed lake drained by the Köl-Sai torrent; burst 23 Jul 2012; sensors since 2016.

name: Muz-Köl
note: Moraine-dammed lake (~3,300 m) at the head of the Muz-Suu; partial outburst night of 22 Jul 2016; sirens kept by clan wardens.

name: Kashka-Suu Glaciers
note: Three valley glaciers (snouts 3,500-3,700 m), area down ~1/4 1970-2018.

name: Tuyuk-Suu Pass
note: Horse-only ~3,400 m pass in the central Talas Alatau between the upper Talas valley and the Chatkal headwaters, marked by cairns.

name: Aksay Plateau
note: ~2,400 km2 syrt at 3,000-3,600 m in the eastern Talas Alatau on the Talas/Uzun-Akmat divide; summer pasture and Kurultai ground.

name: Kurultai ground (Aksay Plateau)
note: Ring of white yurts for the August Kurultai near the Kosh-Döbö camps.

name: Achuu-Köl
note: Bitter sulfate lake at ~3,000 m on the Aksay Plateau, no outlet, no fish.

name: Aksay Border Patrol Post
note: Gendarmerie checkpoint (~2,000 m, 2009) on the line at the lower end of the track to the Aksay Plateau; open on migration dates.

name: Aksay Emergency Shelter
note: Stone hut (1983, restored 2012) below the pass onto the plateau on the tribal side.

name: Otmek Pass
note: Pass (3,330 m) near the eastern end of the Talas Alatau on the old Talas-Suusamyr road; weather station below.

name: Talas River headwaters (Karakol and Uch-Koshoi)
note: Headstreams draining the Kyrgyz Range/Talas Alatau junction below the Otmek Pass, tribal side.

name: Karakol-Ashuu
note: ~3,450 m pass at the head of the Western Karakol valley linking Karakol village with the upper Talas valley; hut rebuilt 2011.

name: Karakol Glacier
note: 4 km valley glacier, snout ~3,400 m below the Karakol-Ashuu track, retreated ~600 m since 1962.

name: Karakol Mountain Logistics Depot
note: Clan-run fuel, flour and fodder base at the end of the all-weather road in the upper Western Karakol valley.

name: Suusamyr Valley
note: High valley (2,000-2,500 m) E of the Talas Alatau draining to the Naryn; main summer pasture of the eastern clans; east end in Kyrgyzstan.

name: Suusamyr Wool Washing Mill
note: Cooperative wool-scouring plant by a warm spring in an old state-farm yard (reopened 2006), Jul-Oct only.

name: Suusamyr earthquake epicentre (1992)
note: M~7.3 quake of 19 Aug 1992 that cracked the Old Quarter mudbrick and the dome of St. Janyl.

name: Aksu-Zhabagly nature reserve
note: Oldest reserve in Central Asia (1926) on the western Talas Alatau; tribal side since 2007, clan wardens.

name: Ak-Suu Canyon
note: 30 km, ~500 m deep limestone canyon within Aksu-Zhabagly with ibex and lammergeier.

name: Ak-Suu Mineral Springs
note: 24 °C carbonated bicarbonate springs at the foot of the canyon; herders bathe in stone pools.

name: Karatau
note: Low limestone/shale range trending NW from the western end of the Talas Alatau, highest ~2,170 m (point placed at its real high summit).

name: Kyzylkum Fringe
note: Desert/semi-desert winter-pasture belt where the Karatau foothills descend toward the Syr Darya; label point; scene of the 2018 border clashes.

name: Kulan-Talaa
note: Wormwood semi-desert plain between the Karatau foothills and the Kyzylkum Fringe (winter pasture).

name: Kulan-Sor
note: 14 x 5 km endorheic salt pan on the Kulan-Talaa, brine in spring, salt crust by July.

name: Karakyr Range
note: Low arid limestone outlier of the Karatau above the Kyzylkum Fringe; autumn raptor migration counts.

name: Kyzyl-Jar badlands
note: Red sandstone cliffs and badlands on the western edge where the Karatau foothills descend to the Kyzylkum Fringe.

name: Kök-Moinok
note: Clay canyon system in the Karatau foothills reached by off-road vehicle from the Talas valley.

name: Teshik-Talaa
note: Karst plateau at ~1,400 m pitted with ~200 sinkholes; spring pasture.

name: Bürküt-Uya
note: 300 m limestone ravine on the northern Karatau slopes with nesting lammergeiers since 1986.

name: Rabat-i Kamal
note: 11th-c. fired-brick Kara-Khanid caravanserai with vaulted cisterns beside Hauzdy on the old Karatau-foothill road west of the Talas valley.

name: Bitik-Tash petroglyphs
note: 400+ Bronze Age/Saka petroglyphs and rock shelters in a ravine above the village.

name: Moiynkum Desert
note: Fixed-dune sand desert between the Chu and the Talas; Boztorgoy winter pastures; label point.

name: Betpak-Dala (southern)
note: Clay and gravel plateau north of the Chu, only its southern edge in Irad; label point.

name: Akzhaykyn Depression
note: Closed basin where the Chu ends in a shallow lake and reedbeds, lowest ground in Irad (<300 m).

name: Keng-Talaa
note: Firm grassland on the southern edge of the Betpak-Dala; course of the annual ~40 km at chabysh.

name: Mazar-Too
note: Isolated granite hill (~1,050 m, 600 m above the steppe) with a stone-piled saint's tomb; offerings before spring migration.

name: Kaz-Köl
note: Shallow saline lakes on the southern Betpak-Dala; flamingo stopover (1,200 in May 2016).

name: Kalmak-Kuduk
note: 180 m borehole (1967) beside a "Dzungar" hand-dug well, solar pump since 2011, waters ~4,000 sheep.

name: Kumdy-Bulak
note: Perennial 2 L/s spring at the foot of the dunes on the southern edge of the Moiynkum, the only water within a day's walk.

name: Muyunkum Natural Gas Field
note: Largest (largely undeveloped) gas prospect beneath the NE Moiynkum near the lower Chu; a few southern-margin wells supply Nurzhan.

name: Talas River terminus
note: The Talas dies out in sands, reed marshes and salt lakes on the western margin of the Moiynkum.

name: Talas border gauge
note: Gauge where the TRHMS and its Kazakh counterpart exchange daily discharge for the 50/50 Talas split; placed where the river leaves the irrigated lower valley.

name: Nurzhan central square
note: Ceremonial square of the 1927 radial plan (city-centre anchor) where Toktarov leaked the Bill of Sale and proclaimed the ISEZ on 25 Feb 2007.

name: House of Soviets (Nurzhan city administration)
note: Constructivist stepped block (1929-32) with window bands on the central square, now the city administration.

name: Azatlık Prospect
note: Main avenue (ex-Lenin Prospect) of granite post-war buildings running from the central square.

name: Palace of Metallurgists
note: Soviet palace of culture (Bolotbek Bekzhanov, 1964) on Azatlık Prospect.

name: Nurzhan Municipal Library
note: Main public library (1931; granite building 1958) on Azatlık Prospect, >300,000 volumes.

name: Nurzhan Polytechnic Institute
note: Ex-Kobozev Polytechnic, foremost technical university (petroleum engineering); main building 1956.

name: NurGaz headquarters
note: HQ of the Nurzhan Oil and Gas Company (Kamran Bekzatov) in the centre.

name: NurGaz Stadium
note: 16,500-seat home of Neftchi (1958 Neftyanik Stadium, renamed 1998); 2014 riot; 31 Oct 2026 Kara-Ak derby.

name: Lokomotiv Stadium
note: Ground of Temirjolchu Nurzhan (railway club), placed by the station.

name: Nurzhan railway station
note: Main junction of Irad Temir Jolu (lines west to Talas, north to Kazakhstan); 1925 congress met at this railway settlement.

name: Nurzhan Rail Freight Depot
note: Main freight yard on the line north to the Kazakh network; tank cars to Shymkent until 2000; railway settlement behind it.

name: Nurzhan Refinery No. 1
note: Only refinery (late 1950s, expanded 1974; 50,000 bpd nameplate, ~31,000 bpd 2023) in the eastern industrial zone.

name: Nurzhan Asphalt and Bitumen Plant
note: Bitumen plant next to the refinery using its heavy residues.

name: Nurzhan ammonia works
note: Chemical works adjacent to the refinery making agricultural ammonia.

name: NurGaz tank farm (Feeder head station)
note: Tank farm "outside the city" receiving the trunk line and heading the 85 km Northern Export Feeder (head pumping station).

name: Attelkom Data Center
note: Data centre (2000s) in the eastern industrial zone with links to Boz-Korgon since 2023.

name: Nurzhan Central Grain Terminal (NAI)
note: Grain silos and feed mills of Nurzhan Agro-Industrial in the eastern industrial zone.

name: Zhetysu Industrial Textiles
note: Wool, felt and cotton-thread spinning sheds in the eastern industrial zone.

name: Xinjiang Lihua spinning complex
note: Spinning complex "near Nurzhan" that receives lint from Lihua gins.

name: Nurzhan Heavy Machine Plant
note: Ex-Kobozev plant (pumpjacks, tanks; 1952 foundry strike), placed by the Dastgoh foundry quarter.

name: NurGaz Pipeline Maintenance Depot
note: Pipeline service base and SCADA control room in Dastgoh District.

name: Dastgoh Creek
note: 3 km canal from a Chu branch through the old foundry quarter (once drove forge hammers).

name: Nurzhan Gas Compressor Station
note: Three-turbine compressor station (1970s) on the northern edge for associated and Muyunkum gas.

name: Nurzhan central heat and power plant
note: Central district-heating plant (coal/gas cogeneration) supplying most of the city.

name: Navbahor Pond
note: 8 ha artificial pond (1998) in Navbahor District fed by a Chu branch canal.

name: Navbahor solar-powered school
name_ru: Школа на солнечной энергии в Навбахоре
note: New school opened by Lt Gov Maksat on 5 Oct 2026 (IS 31.5 m).

name: Nurzhan Botanical Gardens
note: 58 ha garden (1957) on the eastern edge (placed SE to avoid the industrial zone).

name: Nurzhan Municipal Botanical Institute
note: Research institute and gene bank working with the botanical gardens.

name: Nurzhan Children's Polyclinic
note: Main children's outpatient clinic (1961), ~60,000 registered children.

name: Nurzhan Emergency Dispatch Center
note: Unified 2010 dispatch for Nurzhan and Chu District (new building 2016).

name: Nurzhan Technical Lyceum
note: Vocational school (1952), ~900 students placed with NurGaz and the Heavy Machine Plant.

name: St. Teresa Community Kitchen
note: Soup kitchen (1998) of the Latin-rite parish of St. Teresa (Polish/German descent).

name: Nurzhan synagogue and Jewish community center
note: Remaining synagogue and community centre after 1990s emigration.

name: Nurzhan madrasa
note: Small imam-training madrasa opened 1995, run by the muftiate.

name: IradOdin regional studio
note: IradOne's Nurzhan studio producing the Russian-language channel.

name: 2nd Motor Rifle Brigade base
note: MKK brigade in Nurzhan guarding the refinery, pumping stations, Feeder and northern rail links.

name: Chu Basin Hydrological Station
note: River-monitoring station on the Chu at Nurzhan (1932), shares data with Kazakhstan.

name: Chu Correctional Colony
note: Prison colony near Nurzhan (Corrections Directorate).

name: Boz-Korgon compound
note: "Grey Fortress" hardened continuity-of-government site: a walled ~116 ha compound on a spur crest (~890 m) 40 km E of Nurzhan, inside a fenced ~40 km² restricted area along the eastern road-rail corridor; Toktarov residence since 2011, de facto executive seat since 2023; UNMI barred.

name: Chu Gate crossing
note: Main road-freight crossing into Kazakhstan at the end of the Chu highway east of Nurzhan (2008 protocol).

name: Nurzhan rail border station
name_ir: Nurzhan temir jol chek ara bekety
note: Rail-only frontier station at the end of the north line (the Turksib east of Nurzhan), on the Kazakh frontier towards Otar, where crews and customs of both sides exchange trains with Kazakhstan Temir Zholy.

name: Kum-Shagyl crossing
note: Seasonal crossing for farm/local traffic set up by the 2008 protocol; location not given, placed on the Chu-plain frontier NE of Nurzhan.

name: Northern Export Feeder metering station
note: Custody-transfer metering station on the eastern Kazakh frontier 85 km NE of the tank farm, into KazTransOil.

name: Chu oil fields
note: NurGaz sweet light crude fields of the lower Chu (discovered 1949; 48,000-120,000 bpd), wells along the Uzun-Kyr anticline NW of Nurzhan.

name: Uzun-Kyr
note: 28 km, 120 m low anticlinal ridge NW of Nurzhan with oil wells on its crest since the 1950s.

name: NurGaz main field collection station
note: Main field collection station NW (WNW) of Nurzhan in the Chu District fields, head of the ~90 km Nurzhan Petroleum Pipeline.

name: Shahr-i Buzurg
note: Sogdian/Kara-Khanid walled town (6th-12th c.) ~30 km W of Nurzhan beside Shaar-Döbö; protected 1979.

name: Diz-i Zard
note: Kara-Khanid citadel mound refortified by Kokand in the 1820s, taken by Russia 1860-62; in Sary-Döbö village, lower Chu.

name: Shahr-i Nav ruins
note: Ruins of a small Kara-Khanid town that gave its name to the 1962 state-farm village north of Nurzhan.

name: Chui Sugar Refining Corporation factory (Besh-Terek)
note: 1950s beet-sugar works near Besh-Terek W of Nurzhan, privatized 1997.

name: Chui Cotton Inspection Directorate laboratories
note: Cotton grading and quarantine laboratories at Besh-Terek.

name: Xinjiang Lihua Ginning Mill No. 3
note: Former Soviet gin in the lower Chu valley re-equipped 2018.

name: Kök-Döbö weather radar
note: ISEZ hydromet weather radar (2008) on the hill above Kök-Döbö SE of Nurzhan.

name: Sary-Kyr
note: Loess ridge ~200 m above the plain on the southern side of the Chu lowlands; raptor updrafts.

name: Boz-Suu diversion weir
note: 1958 weir diverting most of the 48 km Boz-Suu into the Chu canal system.

name: Kyzyl-Suu (Chu tributary)
note: Red-silt mudflow-prone river from the western Kyrgyz Range diverted onto its alluvial fan.

name: Chu Irrigation Canal System headworks
note: Main intake of the ~1,200 km lower-Chu canal network (>80,000 ha) where the Chu enters the ISEZ lowlands; position not given.

name: Chu River (entry into Irad)
note: Where the Chu, after the Orto-Sai-regulated Chuy valley and the Kazakh border reach, enters the Iradi lowlands.

name: Uch-Terek Rapids
note: 6 km grade III-IV rapids on the Naryn above the head of the reservoir; summer rafting from Talas.

name: Naryn River (entry into Irad)
note: The Naryn enters Irad through deep gorges on the eastern edge of the Toktogul-Naryn zone.

name: Naryn River (leaving Irad)
note: Below the Lower Naryn stations the river emerges onto the Fergana Valley and leaves Irad for Uzbekistan.

name: Uzun-Akmat River (mouth)
note: ~100 km river from the eastern Talas Alatau/Aksay entering the Toktogul Reservoir near Ozgörüsh.

name: Uzun-Akmat Terraces
note: Dry-stone terraces climbing 200 m above the lower valley around Ozgörüsh (vines, apricots, walnuts).

name: Tar-Kapchygai
note: 12 km granite gorge on the middle Uzun-Akmat with birch-rowan woods.

name: Ak-Muz
note: Permanent snowfield (3,800-4,100 m, ~6 km2) on the southern slopes of the eastern Talas Alatau above the upper Uzun-Akmat.

name: Koi-Bel
note: 2,680 m pack-horse pass on a Fergana Range ridge above the Toktogul basin; up to 20,000 sheep a season.

name: Kök-Art Pass
note: Summer-only pass over the Fergana Range at the head of the Kök-Art valley on the Fergana Rim / Toktogul-Naryn boundary.

name: Fergana Range
note: Range on Irad's SE margin above the Toktogul basin and the Fergana Valley; label point.

name: Arslanbob walnut-fruit forest
note: Among the world's largest walnut forests (1,000-2,000 m) on the SW slopes of Babash-Ata.

name: Arslanbob Falls (great waterfall)
note: ~80 m waterfall above the forest; visitor fee.

name: Arslanbob Falls (small waterfall)
note: ~25 m waterfall close to the village.

name: Shrine of Arslanbob-Ata
note: Muslim shrine with a mosque beside it in Arslanbob village, pilgrimage from the Fergana Valley.

name: Babash-Ata Ridge
note: Fergana Range spur rising over 4,000 m behind Arslanbob.

name: Kara-Unkur Cave
note: Limestone cave with Middle/Upper Palaeolithic layers and wild-horse bones in the Kara-Unkur valley above Bazar-Korgon.

name: Bazar-Korgon bazaar
note: Main Fergana Rim market and cross-line smuggling node (Chubar clan).

name: Mailuu-Suu uranium tailings
note: Two dozen Soviet uranium tailings dumps (1946-68) in a landslide-prone valley; 1958 dam failure; basis of the no-uranium pledge.

name: Kök-Kamar Gorge
note: 7 km limestone/shale canyon on a right-bank Kara-Darya tributary, walnut-gatherers' path.

name: Kum-Say Fan
note: ~90 km2 alluvial fan on the eastern rim (cotton, orchards; water disputes with Uzbek villages).

name: Tuura-Say
note: Dry wash on the northern rim; May 2005 mudflow, gabion check dams 2014.

name: Chopo-Jar
note: Red/yellow Neogene clay bluffs near Sopol-Tepa dug by potters.

name: Sadaf-Jar
note: Sandstone bluffs with fossil oyster beds on the northern rim.

name: Kichi-Bel
note: Lowest (1,950 m) crossing of a Fergana Range spur between the northern rim and the valleys to the NW; early-spring route.

name: Jangak-Bulak sacred walnut grove
note: Very old walnuts by the spring, visited by both Muslims (rags) and Syro-Iradi Christians; west of Arslanbob.

name: Chatkal Range
note: ~200 km range branching SW from the Talas Alatau, >4,000 m; label point.

name: Chatkal River (middle valley)
note: ~220 km river draining the trough between the Talas Alatau and Chatkal range SW to Charvak (Uzbekistan).

name: Chatkal Gorge
note: ~60 km canyon of the lower Chatkal (walls >500 m, grade IV-V rapids) ending at the Uzbek border.

name: Lake Sary-Chelek
note: Landslide-dammed lake (7.5 km, 234 m deep) in the Kojo-Ata valley.

name: Sary-Chelek Biosphere Reserve (Arkyt HQ)
note: 23,868 ha MAB reserve (1959/1978) on the southern Chatkal slopes, HQ at Arkyt at its southern entrance.

name: Chatkal Snow Leopard Sanctuary
note: ~45,000 ha of high eastern Chatkal range managed by clan pasture committees (~a dozen snow leopards).

name: Kök-Jar Pass
note: ~3,100 m scree/permafrost horse pass above Kök-Jar near the Uzbek border, watched by Uzbek guards.

name: Kök-Jar antimony exploration mine (disused)
note: Soviet adits, dumps and ore kiln about 4 km down the valley from the village; worked until the early 1990s.

name: Kök-Jar Primary School
note: Four-classroom school (1966) at the old mine camp about 5 km below the village, Iradi-only since 2008.

name: Terek-Sai mines
note: Soviet gold and antimony mines worked from the 1930s to 1991 around the village (headframes, adits).

name: Isyk-Bulak
note: 31 °C springs by old adits near Terek-Sai; arsenic above limits (2019).

name: Ak-Bash
note: Glaciated limestone peak (3,680 m) of the high Chatkal range.

name: Kylych-Kyr
note: About 5 km knife-edge arête running north from Ak-Bash to an unnamed ~4,050 m summit.

name: Kara-Kazan Cirque
note: Granite-walled cirque (floor ~3,500 m) with remnant glacier and lake, reached from Muz-Tör.

name: Besh-Köl Glaciers
note: Five small cirque glaciers (~3 km2, 2015) above the Besh-Köl camp and lakes.

name: Kyzyl-Bel Pass
note: 2,450 m red-sandstone pass over a spur above the upper Chatkal valley (May-Oct).

name: Altyn-Say
note: 22 km gold-bearing stream entering the Chatkal from the south; mercury banned 2012.

name: Ak-Balyk Creek
note: Spring-fed 8 °C trout creek tributary of the Chatkal, line fishing only.

name: Chakmak-Say
note: 18 km seasonal torrent on the western Chatkal slopes near the Uzbek border joining below the main gorges.

name: Kum-Bel gold prospect
note: Soviet-drilled gold-telluride vein prospect below the Kum-Bel ridge (camp to 1991), under the clan moratorium.

name: Jashyl-Köl
note: Green moraine-dammed lake at ~2,600 m on the southern Chatkal slopes with a summer herders' camp.

name: Kök-Bel Pass
note: Paved 2,670 m road pass across the western Kyrgyz Range, short summer route Talas-Chu; often closed in winter; snowplough depot at Toguz-Bulak.

name: Kyrgyz Range (western end)
note: North side of the Talas valley; its western end is rounded by the lowland railway; label point.

name: Talas River (at Talas)
note: 661 km endorheic river flowing W through the capital (braided channel, aryk intakes) then N into the Moiynkum.

name: Otmek Valley Checkpoint
note: Gendarmerie control post at the mouth of the Otmek valley where State Route 1 leaves the Talas valley; heavy vehicles pay the road-use charge here.

name: Kerben Airstrip
note: Soviet 1.8 km strip on the tribal side; Iradiya Twin Otters land here only by consent of the clan council.

name: Kazarman Airstrip
note: Soviet 1.8 km strip above the Naryn gorge; Iradiya Twin Otters land here only by consent of the clan council.

name: Toktogul Airstrip
note: 1 km strip outside Toktogul; no scheduled flights, used by Iradiya charters and medical evacuation.

name: Boz-Korgon Airstrip
note: 1.2 km strip serving the Boz-Korgon compound for government and Iradiya charter aircraft; inside the restricted area.

name: Aulie-Ata Airfield (disused)
note: Soviet regional airport closed in 1994; the 3.5 km runway is used for grain drying and as a diversion field for Talas.

name: Kulan Airfield (disused)
note: Soviet bomber dispersal field near Lugovoy, closed in 1992; inside the restricted-weapons zone since 2007 and inspected by UNMI each quarter.

name: Moiynkum Airfield (disused)
note: Soviet reserve airfield in the desert, abandoned and partly lifted; herders use the apron as a camel-market ground.

name: Karatau phosphorite quarries (disused)
note: Soviet open pits that fed the Aulie-Ata superphosphate works; idle on the tribal side since the 1990s.

name: Kuru-Tegerek copper prospect (disused)
note: Soviet exploration camp on a copper-gold deposit, abandoned in 1991 and kept undeveloped under the clan mining moratorium.

name: Amangeldy gas wells (capped)
note: Soviet exploration wells on a gas-condensate structure, capped in 1991; part of the undeveloped Muyunkum gas province.

name: Kümüshtü tailings (capped)
note: Tailings of a 1970s Soviet silver-lead pilot mill at Shelji, capped in 2012.

name: Toguz-Bulak crossing
note: Qara-Chik line crossing on the Kök-Bel road (central sector): Gendarmerie checkpoint on the ISEZ side, El-Choro post on the tribal side.

name: Toguz-Bulak crossing
note: Qara-Chik line crossing on the Kök-Bel road (central sector): Gendarmerie checkpoint on the ISEZ side, El-Choro post on the tribal side.

name: Kara-Bulak crossing
note: Qara-Chik line crossing on the Kenkol Pass road (western sector): Gendarmerie checkpoint on the ISEZ side, El-Choro post on the tribal side.

name: Suusamyr crossing
note: Qara-Chik line crossing on the Western Karakol valley road (southern sector): Gendarmerie checkpoint on the ISEZ side, El-Choro post on the tribal side.

name: Mailuu-Suu road crossing
note: Qara-Chik line crossing on the Mailuu-Suu road (southern sector): Gendarmerie checkpoint on the ISEZ side, El-Choro post on the tribal side.

name: Arslanbob road crossing
note: Qara-Chik line crossing on the Arslanbob road (southern sector): Gendarmerie checkpoint on the ISEZ side, El-Choro post on the tribal side.
